subject: Acme - Post-call TCO recap and next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>; Priya Singh <priya.singh@acme.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-14T16:05:00-08:00
Subject: Acme - Post-call TCO recap and next steps

Hi Alex & Priya,

Great to meet earlier — thanks for walking through the integration and high-level volume profile. Per our call, I wanted to capture the key pain points, goals, and the cost levers we discussed so your team can share internally. I attached a first-pass TCO model (acme_tco_estimate_v1.xlsx) and a short note on batching/caching assumptions (redwood-batching-notes.pdf).

Summary of what I heard:
- Pain: High per-request cost at current 3B token/month projection, and unpredictable spikes during customer support bursts.
- Goal: Deliver sub-200ms median latency for chat, keep monthly inference spend below $35k for pilot, and validate 30%+ cost improvement over current managed provider.
- Constraints: Security review in 3 weeks (Priya), procurement timeline by end of March, and infra team wants clear reserved vs burst pricing.

Primary cost/TCO levers we recommend for this workload:
1) Token economics: model choice + context window — switching to a LlamaX-13B quantized variant reduces per-token compute by ~38% in our profile (see tab "Model Assumptions").
2) Batching: using continuous batching and a 50ms micro-batching window for async support reduces per-token overhead by ~22% at your 200 QPS spikes.
3) KV prefix caching: for repeated customer prompts (help center lookup), prefix cache hit rates of 40% could shave another ~15% off token counts.
4) Reserved capacity: committing to a small Dedicated pool for predictable baseline throughput plus burst routing to hosted improves unit economics for steady-state traffic.

Next steps I propose:
- Rafael and I can schedule a 30-minute TCO deep-dive with your infra team to walk the attached workbook and assumptions (availability: Tue/Wed next week).
- Priya, we can provide a procurement-friendly estimate and a DocuSign-ready SOW after we align on reserved capacity size.
- Alex, could you confirm the 3B/month projection and share a short list of 3 typical prompt patterns (support chat, knowledge search, triage) so we can tune caching estimates?

If that all looks right I’ll schedule the follow-up and send a short one-page that Procurement can use for the initial review.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | (415) 555-0132
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Acme - Post-call TCO recap and next steps

Thanks Marissa — this is super helpful. Quick clarifications:

- The 3B token/month number is our worst-case for Q3; pilot will probably be ~600M tokens/month but with high burstiness during launches.
- Budget constraint for pilot: target <= $35k/mo, but we can stretch to $45k/mo if we can justify ROI for faster resolution times.
- Prompt patterns: 1) short chat back-and-forth (avg 25 tokens/request), 2) knowledge-base search (longer context, avg 300 tokens/request), 3) triage prompt (system + user, avg 180 tokens).

Rafael — can you include an example reserved capacity config and rough monthly pricing for a 600M token pilot vs a 3B committed model in the deep-dive?

Priya — procurement timeline looks aligned; we’ll likely need the PO estimate and security overview in the next two weeks.

Appreciate the follow-up — let us know your availability.

—Alex
Alex Johnson
Director of Product, Acme Corp
alex.johnson@acme.com

Thanks Alex — got it. Quick notes from QE/pricing side before the deep-dive: 

- Reserved vs burst example (ballpark):
  * Pilot reserved pool sized for 50% of average steady-state usage + burst routing (usage above reserved billed at a higher per-token rate).
  * For a 600M pilot profile, reserved capacity that handles ~300M productive tokens/month plus burst gives the best cost predictability.
  * We can offer a 10-15% committed usage discount on a 12-month reserved plan; short-term pilots (1–3 months) typically get smaller discounts but we can negotiate pilot credits.

- Technical hooks: we’ll show how batching window and cache-hit assumptions influence cost per effective token in the workbook. Rafael to walk the math.

Rafael Mendes
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
rafael@redwood.com
